target.title: fix(browser): apply profile proxy policy to tab list redaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
`/tabs` and `/tabs/action` list redaction only used the global SSRF policy. They did not include the selected profile's browser proxy mode, while tab open/focus/select already use `browserNavigationPolicyForProfile`.

## Why This Change Was Made
Strict browser navigation policy depends on whether the browser profile itself is proxy-routed. Tab list URL redaction is a navigation-result policy check, so it should receive the same profile-aware policy as the other tab routes.

## User Impact
Tab list responses now redact URLs consistently for proxy-routed browser profiles instead of evaluating them with an incomplete policy. This keeps list responses aligned with focus/select safety checks.

## Evidence
- Changed tab list redaction to accept `browserNavigationPolicyForProfile(ctx, profileCtx)`.
- Added route regression coverage for both `/tabs` and `/tabs/action list` passing `explicit-browser-proxy` into result guards.
- Added attach-only route proof in `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts` that uses the real browser route context and real navigation guard: strict SSRF plus `--proxy-server=...` redacts a public IP-literal tab URL for both list endpoints.
- Focused tests:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
  - Result: 2 files / 24 tests passed.
- Touched-file checks:
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts`
  - `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`
- Autoreview closeout:
  - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude --prompt '<scope prompt>'`
  - Result: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Proof
The original route regression verifies the policy object passed to the redaction guard. The attach-only regression now exercises the same route handlers with the real navigation guard and a loopback OpenClaw CDP profile configured with `--proxy-server=...`; under strict SSRF, the tab list response keeps the tab identity but blanks the URL for both `GET /tabs` and `POST /tabs/action { action: "list" }`. This proof does not require a live proxy or credentials because the changed behavior is the preflight navigation-result policy decision before any browser network request.

target.title: fix(workboard): check active claim before dependency status guard in claim()
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #104050 — `claim()` checks the dependency status guard (card status must be `"ready"`) before checking whether the card is already claimed. Since a successful claim moves the card to `"running"`, any repeat claim on a card with parents returns the misleading error `"card dependencies are not done"` instead of `"card already claimed by <owner>"`.

Cards without parents are unaffected — only the misordered dependency guard triggers this false error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Swap the order of two guards in `claim()`: check the active claim lease before the dependency status guard. The existing claim check (`already claimed by`) and dependency check (`dependencies are not done`) each remain correct on their own; the fix is purely about which one runs first.

No status transitions, no new error messages, no API changes — just moving `existingClaim` above `cardParentIds`.

**Test correction (`fbb9293dc5`):** the regression test first pushed here built the parent link through raw `metadata.links`, which `create()` strips (parent/child dependencies must go through `linkCards`). The child was therefore parentless, the dependency guard never fired, and the test passed with *or* without the fix. It now builds a real dependency via `linkCards` + `promoteReady` and asserts the link and promotion, so it genuinely guards the ordering (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix).

## User Impact

Agents that repeat-claim a dependency-backed card now see the correct `"already claimed by <owner>"` error instead of a misleading `"dependencies not done"` that sends them into dependency-debugging loops.

## Evidence

### Real runtime behavior (SQLite-backed `WorkboardStore`)

Reproduced #104050 end-to-end against a real `node:sqlite` store (not the in-memory test double), driving the public store API — build a parent→child dependency with `linkCards`, mark the parent `done`, `promoteReady`, then claim the child twice. `before` = pre-fix (`HEAD~1`), `after` = this fix.

```
########## BEFORE (pre-fix) ##########
setup   child.parents=[<cardId>] child.status=ready
claim#1 owner=main   -> status=running  token=<redacted>
claim#2 owner=other  -> Error: card dependencies are not done.     # misleading

########## AFTER (this fix) ##########
setup   child.parents=[<cardId>] child.status=ready
claim#1 owner=main   -> status=running  token=<redacted>
claim#2 owner=other  -> Error: card already claimed by main.       # correct
```

<details><summary>Repro driver (throwaway, not committed)</summary>

```ts
import { mkdtempSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { WorkboardStore } from "./extensions/workboard/src/store.ts";
import { createWorkboardSqliteStores } from "./extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.ts";

const s = createWorkboardSqliteStores({
  dbPath: join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "wb-")), "workboard.sqlite"),
});
const store = new WorkboardStore(s.cards, {
  boards: s.boards, subscriptions: s.subscriptions, attachments: s.attachments,
});

const parent = await store.create({ title: "Parent A", status: "todo" });
const child  = await store.create({ title: "Child B",  status: "todo" });
await store.linkCards(parent.id, child.id);          // real parent->child dependency
await store.update(parent.id, { status: "done" });
await store.promoteReady();                          // child -> ready

const first = await store.claim(child.id, { ownerId: "main", ttlSeconds: 60 });
console.log("claim#1 ->", first.card.status);        // running
try { await store.claim(child.id, { ownerId: "other" }); }
catch (e) { console.log("claim#2 ->", e.message); }
```

</details>

### Regression test (now effective)

The corrected test fails on the pre-fix guard order and passes after the fix:

```
# new test @ FIXED store.ts
  Tests  1 passed

# new test @ PRE-FIX store.ts (HEAD~1)
  × reports already claimed instead of dependency error for a claimed dependency-backed card
  AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error matching /already claimed/
    but got 'card dependencies are not done.'
```

### Full suite + lint

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  80 passed (80)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts
  exit 0
```

1 production line moved + 1 effective regression test. Bounded to `extensions/workboard/src/`. No config, SDK, CLI, docs, or changelog surface was added.

target.title: fix(web-media): add timeoutMs option to WebMediaOptions for remote fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadWebMedia` / `readRemoteMediaBuffer` had no upper bound on header-arrival latency. An unresponsive upstream could pin a Tlon media download or URL-backed image upload at the TCP/streaming-read layer until `readIdleTimeoutMs` finally tripped — and only if a body ever started. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through `WebMediaOptions` and the two Tlon call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — replaces the prior "aborts a … via the overall timeoutMs deadline" test with **"forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer"** (using `vi.useFakeTimers()` + a progressing body stream, identical to main's `fetch.test.ts:438-485` "clears the response-header deadline while a healthy body keeps progressing" pattern). Asserts the resolved buffer contains the enqueued bytes after the header deadline clears — proving the public seam actually forwards the field.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` — replaces `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `downloadMedia`'s `fetchOptions` now forwards `responseHeaderTimeoutMs:` to both `saveRemoteMedia` and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`.
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` — replaces `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `uploadImageFromUrl`'s `readRemoteMediaBuffer` call forwards the same.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts` — assertion relaxed to `expect.objectContaining({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })`.
- `proof-103206-tool-run.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end (real stalled HTTP server + real `loadWebMedia` + real AbortSignal + surfaced error shape).

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for Tlon media downloads and URL-backed image uploads triggered by `extensions/tlon`.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (30s for Tlon) continues to bound chunk gaps. This is the deliberate behavior change vs. the prior total-timeout proposal.
- Tlon users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape)

Local fallback run (Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-103206-tool-run.mts
[proof] stalled HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:36539
[proof] calling loadWebMedia with responseHeaderTimeoutMs=1000ms (production code path uses 15*60_000)
[proof] this exercises the canonical seam from PR #103020:
[proof]   loadWebMedia -> readRemoteMediaBuffer -> fetchGuardedMediaResponse
[proof]   -> fetchWithSsrFGuard -> buildTimeoutAbortSignal (response header deadline)
[proof]   -> globalThis.fetch
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 1000ms (elapsed 1001ms) operation=media response headers url=http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png
[proof] elapsed: 1154ms
[proof] surfaced error.name: MediaFetchError
[proof] surfaced error.code: fetch_failed
[proof] surfaced error.message: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out
[proof] surfaced error.cause.name: TimeoutError
[proof] surfaced error.cause.message: request timed out
[proof] result: responseHeaderTimeoutMs fired through real production path
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png",
  "responseHeaderTimeoutMs": 1000,
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "error",
    "name": "MediaFetchError",
    "code": "fetch_failed",
    "message": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out",
    "causeName": "TimeoutError",
    "causeMessage": "request timed out",
    "elapsedMs": 1154
  },
  "passed": true
}
```

Key observations:
- **1154ms elapsed** (vs 1000ms `responseHeaderTimeoutMs`): the `[fetch-timeout]` log fires at the deadline, proving the AbortSignal fires at the configured header deadline.
- **Surfaced error shape**: `MediaFetchError { code: "fetch_failed", cause: TimeoutError("request timed out") }` — the exact error shape that propagates to the Tlon extension caller.

### Repository test (forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs through the public seam)

Added in `src/media/web-media.test.ts > loadWebMedia > forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer`. The test uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` and an `enqueue([1],25) → enqueue([2],50) → close(75)` body stream (matching main's pattern at `fetch.test.ts:438-485`). Asserts the resolved buffer equals the concatenation of enqueued bytes — proving the header deadline is cleared on success and the body keeps progressing past it.

Focused suite runs (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

### Canonical precedents

- **PR #103020 / merge `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`** — `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` at `src/media/fetch.ts:82`; the canonical seam. Implements header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed on success so the body is not capped.
- **PR #103266 / merge `541c9f0bf01712d81d5217eb2a5c15d05686259d`** — canonical 15-minute bounded-media ceiling from `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`. This PR reuses the same ceiling on the narrower header-only deadline.
- **Telegram precedent** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.ts:356` already uses `TELEGRAM_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`. This PR's constant names mirror that pattern.

## Coordination with #103209

With the canonical seam now on `origin/main`, both this PR and #103209 independently use that seam — they no longer duplicate each other and either can land in any order. No cross-repo stacking required. Each branch typechecks standalone; the `forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer` test on this branch and the equivalent proof path on #103209 cover the same end-to-end contract from different call sites (Tlon vs. agent-tools).

target.title: fix(shell): resolve pwsh.exe/.cmd/.bat on PATH for Windows shell discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, PowerShell 7 delivered via the Microsoft Store / App Execution Alias (and most portable installs) ships as `pwsh.exe`. `resolvePowerShellPath()` step 3 calls `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")`, which only probed a **bare** `pwsh` with no extension. `fs.accessSync(entry/pwsh)` therefore returned `ENOENT`, so shell discovery fell through to Windows PowerShell 5.1 instead of using pwsh 7. This is the actual Windows pwsh resolution gap (distinct from the custom-shell `-c` args discussion in #104053).

## Evidence

Local reproduction on this Windows host (PowerShell 7.6.3 present only as the Store `pwsh.exe` alias, no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`):
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh")` -> `ENOENT` (bare name missed by discovery)
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh.exe")` -> `OK` (extension probe hits it)
- After the fix, `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")` returns the `pwsh.exe` path on PATH, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over the 5.1 fallback.

This matches the source-level analysis: current main only looks for a bare `pwsh`, so a PATH entry containing only `pwsh.exe` is skipped before the Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback (noted by the ClawSweeper review). The PR also adds Windows-only regression tests (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected): finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent, prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1.

(Private paths and credentials redacted; this is a local OpenClaw gateway host.)

## Root cause

`resolveShellFromPath` joined the entry with the bare name and never tried executable extensions on Windows:

```ts
const candidate = path.join(entry, name); // only "pwsh", never "pwsh.exe"
```

## Fix

On `win32`, also probe `.exe`, mirroring the existing pattern already used by `resolveWindowsBashPath` (`"bash.exe"` / `"bash"`).

```ts
const executableExtensions = process.platform === "win32" ? [".exe"] : [];
const candidates = [base, ...executableExtensions.map((ext) => base + ext)];
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex-backed turn hits the subscription usage limit, the Codex harness
returns a `promptError` in the attempt result instead of throwing. The host's
model fallback is throw-driven — it only engages when `FailoverError` is thrown.

The existing prompt-error handler already classifies the error and enters
`resolveRunFailoverDecision`.  However `shouldRotatePrompt` always returns true
for rate/billing limits, so the handler first tries **auth profile rotation** —
retrying the same harness with a different profile.  For harness-owned transports
(Codex) the limit is on the harness session, not the profile, so every rotation
fails identically.  This wastes the user's quota and burns retry budget
before fallback can engage.

Fixes #103734.

## Why This Change Was Made

One 8-line addition in `shouldRotatePrompt` (`failover-policy.ts`): when a
plugin harness owns the transport **and** the failover reason is `rate_limit`
or `billing`, skip profile rotation.  The decision falls through to
`fallback_model` in `resolveRunFailoverDecision`, which throws a `FailoverError`
that the outer fallback loop catches immediately.

Non-harness providers and non-limit errors are unchanged — they still rotate
profiles before falling back.

## User Impact

**Before:** Codex usage limit → profile rotation → all profiles fail →
run budget exhausted or model fallback with wasted quota.

**After:** Codex usage limit → `rate_limit` → skips rotation → falls back
to next configured model immediately.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion. Additionally, a very long decimal `Content-Length`
(e.g., 400+ digits) causes `Number.parseInt` to return `Infinity`, which
was stored as an infinite drain counter — permanently suppressing all
future LSP output and leaving pending requests to time out.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly. For non-safe integer lengths
(`Infinity` from `parseInt`), the arithmetic computed `bodyStart + Infinity
= Infinity`, storing an infinite `oversizeDrainRemaining` that never
decrements. Additionally, when the final drain chunk exactly matched the
remaining byte count, the handler returned early without failing the
session, leaving the pending request to time out.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body when the frame is completely buffered, or tracks
remaining bytes to skip via `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body
arrives across chunks. Non-safe integer Content-Length values (Infinity)
are detected before drain arithmetic and signal a fatal protocol error.
Finite oversized frames (>10 MB but still a safe integer) trigger session
failure after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame — the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead of
waiting for the normal request timeout. The exact-match drain completion
boundary (`raw.length === oversizeDrainRemaining`) now falls through to
the session failure check instead of returning early.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param
  with `fatal` flag; on oversized frames drains the full frame or signals
  remaining bytes and sets the fatal flag. On non-safe integer
  Content-Length signals a fatal condition via NaN.
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer. Detects non-finite
  drain remaining or drained finite oversized frames and calls
  `failLspSession` after dispatching any completed responses parsed
  before the bad header. Fixed the exact-match drain boundary: changed
  `<=` to `<` so the exact-match case continues into session failure.
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`,
  `oversizeDrainSeen: boolean`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now closes three gaps:
1) fully drains finite oversized Content-Length frames (>10 MB) to
prevent memory exhaustion, 2) fails the session for non-safe integer
Content-Length (Infinity from parseInt) instead of permanently suppressing
all future LSP output, and 3) fails the session for finite oversized
frames after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame so the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead
of timing out.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 18 tests pass, including 4 new
handler-level tests for finite oversized Content-Length session failure.

**Before-fix behavior (if applicable)**: Finite oversized frames (>10 MB)
were silently drained without failing the session, leaving the associated
pending request to time out after 10 seconds instead of failing
immediately. When the final drain chunk exactly matched the remaining
oversized body bytes, the handler returned early with a zero counter
without failing the session.

**After-fix evidence**:

All 18 tests pass:
```text
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > oversized Content-Length handling (2)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > unsafe Content-Length handling (4)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > finite oversized Content-Length handling (4)
   ✓ sets fatal flag on parseLspMessages oversizeDrain
   ✓ fails LSP session on finite oversized frame through runtime handler path
   ✓ dispatches valid response before failing session on finite oversized frame
   ✓ fails the session when the final drain chunk exactly completes
```

**Real LSP server evidence**:

Tested against `vscode-json-languageserver` via stdio:

**Terminal output**:
```text
============================================================
L2 EVIDENCE: Real LSP server session via Content-Length framing
Server: vscode-json-languageserver
============================================================
Frame #1: {
  "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "capabilities": {
      "textDocumentSync": 2, "hoverProvider": true,
      "documentSymbolProvider": true, "foldingRangeProvider": true,
      "selectionRangeProvider": true
    }
  }
}
Frame #2: { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": null }
----------------------------------------
Initialize returned capabilities: ✅
Completion responded: ✅
CONCLUSION: Real LSP server session works end-to-end ✅
```

This proves the LSP message parser correctly handles real server I/O
with proper Content-Length framing.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending non-safe Content-Length
or oversized (>10 MB) values — these are protocol violations that no
well-behaved LSP server would produce. The code paths are exercised
through handler-level tests that use the identical `handleIncomingData`
path the production LSP session uses.

**Risk level**: Low — non-safe and finite oversized Content-Length values
both trigger session failure after dispatching valid responses. All
existing message sizes within the 10 MB limit use the unchanged happy
path. merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 18 tests pass
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none

target.title: fix(agents): CJK-aware tool-result truncation budgets
target.body:
Closes #103847

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with CJK-heavy tool results (Chinese, Japanese, Korean text) would keep oversized tool payloads in the agent context even though those results already consumed far more tokens than the live truncation budget intended. Dense CJK was measured by raw UTF-16 length while the budget assumed ~4 Latin characters per token, so content could under-count by up to ~4× and skip truncation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Split live tool-result budgets into two units:

1. **Estimated / token-share** (`maxTokens * 4`) — compared with CJK-aware `estimateStringChars` so dense CJK triggers truncation at the intended token share.
2. **Physical UTF-16 ceiling** — configured `toolResultMaxChars` and the auto hard-cap ladder stay physical-character contracts (not re-interpreted as estimated chars).

When truncating multi-block results, convert each block’s estimated share back to a physical UTF-16 slice budget, clamp `minKeep` to that adjusted allocation (so small caps cannot retain more estimated cost than budgeted), keep short sibling marker blocks intact, and skip empty text blocks so inflation ratios never become NaN. Runtime paths (`run` / `attempt` / session tool-result guard) pass dual budgets via `resolveLiveToolResultBudgets`.

## User Impact

- CJK-heavy tool sessions truncate at the intended context share instead of retaining near-full CJK payloads that pressure the model window.
- Existing `toolResultMaxChars` config remains a **physical** character ceiling (upgrade-compatible).
- Pure ASCII behavior stays the same under the dual-budget path.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Head: `879763fc08a9` (`fix(agents): dual-budget CJK tool-result truncation` on top of `031f85927`)

```text

  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts \
  src/utils/cjk-chars.test.ts \
```

- configured physical ceiling not treated as estimated (CJK keep > ~config/4)
- full CJK payload kept when estimated budget is loose and physical config allows

```json
  "cjk_would_truncate_main": false,
  "cjk_would_truncate_fixed": true
}
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Live tool-result truncation weights dense CJK for automatic token-share budgets while preserving configured physical character ceilings; min-keep no longer defeats CJK-adjusted physical allocations under small caps.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout on branch `fix/103847-cjk-tool-result-truncation` @ `879763fc08a9`, Node + `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.

- What was not tested: Live multi-turn embedded agent run against a real provider with production CJK tool output (provider transcript redaction); non-macOS hosts.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

target.title: fix(tools-manager): bound GitHub releases response body to prevent unbounded read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent helper-tool fallback for `fd` and `ripgrep` read GitHub's latest-release response with `Response.json()`. That consumes the complete remote body before parsing it, so a faulty or compromised response could grow agent memory without a bound.

The affected path is `ensureTool`, reached by the agent `find` and `grep` tools when no suitable local binary is available. The unbounded behavior shipped in `v2026.5.28`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer candidate reads the response through the shared `@openclaw/media-core/read-response-with-limit` helper with an owner-local 1 MiB cap. The two current GitHub responses are about 37 KiB and 51 KiB, leaving more than 20x headroom without importing the provider setup helper's unrelated 16 MiB policy.

The implementation also:

- distinguishes overflow, malformed JSON, missing/invalid `tag_name`, abort, release-status, and download-status failures;
- cancels oversized bodies and always releases the guarded response in `finally`;
- propagates failures from silent automatic resolution so `find`/`grep` report the actionable cause instead of masking corruption as a generic missing tool;
- preserves non-silent log-and-return behavior and existing system/local fallback behavior.

A `Content-Length` check alone would not protect chunked responses, and changing the shared helper or a global cap would broaden the owner boundary unnecessarily.

## User Impact

Oversized or corrupt release metadata can no longer be buffered without limit or silently converted into an ambiguous tool-not-found result. Normal release lookup and download behavior is unchanged. There is no public API, configuration, schema, or documentation change.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `e50b5e1eaf63f4b39d4cda591d4b0262c306112d`

- Local focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 11/11 passed.
- Controlled streaming proof: the exact `ensureTool` resolution path, with the guarded-fetch boundary pointed at a real loopback HTTP endpoint, received a 16 MiB chunked response with no `Content-Length`; it rejected at 1 MiB, canceled/released the response, and never attempted the download.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kweaqrav2snpcn8mfcymje14`: exact-candidate focused proof 11/11; touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, changed guards, and core production typecheck passed. Hydration run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28502391247
- Broad core test typecheck has four unrelated failures; all four reproduce unchanged on merge base `b63e06f68aa0f5fc3dc809c37615b8b1012b180b`.
- Fresh autoreview in local mode and final branch mode: zero accepted/actionable findings.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit.

Original report and starting patch by @sheyanmin. Maintainer follow-up by @steipete/Codex preserves that contributor credit.

<details>
<summary>Security and Privacy</summary>

- Removes an unbounded read from an external response.
- Keeps the existing SSRF/guarded-fetch boundary.
- Logs no response content and adds no persistence or dependency.
- Stream cancellation and response release are covered on failure paths.

</details>

---

AI-assisted. The original proposal and tests were authored with Claude Code (Anthropic) and reviewed by the contributor. The maintainer follow-up, boundary analysis, implementation repair, tests, and verification were performed with OpenAI Codex and reviewed through the repository's autoreview workflow.

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a resumed session's agent run could lose its managed worktree checkout mid-run: idle GC or a separate remover could delete the session's isolated checkout while the run was using it, destroying in-flight workspace files. It also fixes the silent counterpart, where a session whose managed worktree had already been removed was admitted anyway and ran without its checkout as if it were an ordinary directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease, and agent command preparation acquires it as soon as the session cwd resolves, before any workspace-dependent step, releasing it in the run's outer cleanup. The lease retains the existing PID-tagged Git worktree lock with local reference counting, so both same-process removal paths and separate-service removers are excluded while a run is active. Admission for a cwd that belongs to a removed managed worktree now fails with `managed worktree was removed: <path>` instead of proceeding. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics.

## User Impact

Users resuming sessions with isolated worktrees can no longer have their live checkout deleted underneath an active run by idle GC or session cleanup, including when the session works in a subdirectory of the worktree. A session whose checkout was removed while it was away now fails fast with a clear error instead of silently continuing without its files.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `origin/main` (67e1d43911), resolving the `WorktreeSnapshotError` conflict in `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts` in favor of the typed error from main.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/command/worktree-lease.test.ts`: 32 passed, including a new removed-path admission regression.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.worktree-race.test.ts`: 2 passed; the composed regression pauses real preparation while removal races, covering both the run-wins ordering and the removal-wins-before-admission ordering.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`: 35 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.acp.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`: 102 passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on all changed files: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`: clean.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session's agent run must keep its managed worktree checkout while cleanup or a separate remover races it, and a session whose managed worktree was already removed must fail admission instead of silently running in a recreated ordinary directory.
Real environment tested: the production agent command preparation path and ManagedWorktreeService driven end to end on a clean AWS machine (Crabbox lease cbx_619103fb2076, c7a.xlarge), with real on-disk git repositories, real managed worktree creation, and real registry state, comparing pristine main 67e1d43911 against this patch f12f79032a on identical inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `crabbox run --provider aws --id cbx_619103fb2076 --shell -- "bash run.sh"`, where the script creates a session-owned worktree with a nested workspace directory, seeds the session with that cwd, admits the run through the production preparation entry point, races a separate service's non-force removal, releases the run, then removes a second worktree and attempts admission for it again.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 67e1d43911)
# scenario 1: separate remover races an admitted session run
session admitted with nested managed cwd: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: false
nested session directory exists after the removal attempt: false
run admission holds a releasable worktree lease: false
removal after the session run ends: error: unknown active worktree: b4242765-4c49-4ddc-934d-69698e802427
# scenario 2: removal wins before session admission
managed checkout removed before admission: true
session preparation proceeded without its managed worktree: true
preparation still points at the removed cwd: true
# AFTER (this patch f12f79032a, identical inputs)
# scenario 1: separate remover races an admitted session run
session admitted with nested managed cwd: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: true
nested session directory exists after the removal attempt: true
run admission holds a releasable worktree lease: true
removal after the session run ends: removed
# scenario 2: removal wins before session admission
managed checkout removed before admission: true
session preparation fails with: managed worktree was removed: /tmp/openclaw-proof-bvGt15/.openclaw/worktrees/861311bf01e8bf89/proof-removed
managed checkout recreated as ordinary directory: false
```
Observed result after fix: an admitted run holds a releasable lease backed by the live worktree lock, a separate non-force remover is rejected while the run is active and succeeds after the run ends, and admission for a removed managed path fails with a clear error instead of proceeding without its checkout.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the two racing services ran in one process on the remote machine, with cross-process protection relying on the directly verified on-disk Git worktree lock.

target.title: fix(usage): reclaim refresh locks leaked by the current process (#103910)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway usage-cost` can get stuck with `cacheStatus.status: "refreshing"` indefinitely: `pendingFiles` never drain, `refreshedAt` goes stale, and repeated queries hours apart return byte-identical responses frozen at an old `updatedAt`. Root cause: usage-cost refreshes serialize on a pid-stamped lock file (`.usage-cost-cache.json.lock`) whose staleness check trusts **pid-liveness alone** (`isUsageCostCacheRefreshRunning` → `isProcessRunning(lock.pid)`). A lock leaked by the gateway's **own process** — e.g. an in-process SIGUSR1 restart abandoning a mid-refresh promise before its `finally` releases, exactly the long-lived systemd deployment in the report — holds a pid that stays alive for the process's whole lifetime, so every subsequent `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath` returns `"busy"` forever while the background queue keeps re-scheduling. Fixes #103910.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track lock tokens held by this process in a module-level in-memory set: `acquire` registers the token, `release` removes it. The staleness check now reclaims a lock stamped with **our own pid whose token has no live in-process holder** (including tokenless legacy locks) — that lock cannot represent a running refresh in this process. Cross-process locks keep the existing pid-liveness semantics unchanged; genuinely running refreshes (registered token) are still respected. No new options or public surface.

## User Impact

`usage-cost` recovers by itself after a leaked lock instead of serving an aging snapshot that permanently claims to be "refreshing" — the failure mode that let a $1k+/month spend go unnoticed in the linked reports.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression test — forge a lock with `pid: process.pid` and an unregistered token (the leaked-self-lock state), then request a refresh:

```
main:     AssertionError: expected 'busy' to be 'refreshed'   ← stuck forever
this PR:  70/70 passed — lock reclaimed, refresh proceeds
```

The pre-existing "respects live usage cache locks even when they are old" test was retargeted to a genuinely foreign live pid (`process.ppid`), preserving its original intent under the new same-pid contract. Full suite `session-cost-usage.test.ts` 70/70; `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: feat(auto-reply): add "commentary" verbose level for narration-only progress
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/verbose on` is all-or-nothing: an operator following an agent's work in chat gets the useful inter-tool narration (the 💬 preamble commentary) inseparably bundled with per-tool summary lines and plugin/MCP tool posts. For someone tracking *what the agent is thinking*, the tool feed is noise — but the only way to silence it also silences the narration. Closes #103170.

## Why This Change Was Made

The narration and the tool posts are already independent delivery paths in the dispatch layer; they were just wired to a single boolean. This change resolves each verbose level **once** into per-kind lanes — `{ commentary, toolSummaries, toolOutput }` via `resolveVerboseKinds()` in `src/auto-reply/thinking.shared.ts` — and points each existing consumer (dispatch, the followup/embedded runners, gateway chat events, TUI rendering, the `/status` card, the Control UI) at its specific lane instead of a scattered `level === "on" || level === "full"` comparison.

A fourth preset, **`commentary`**, enables only the narration lane. The change is strictly additive: `off | on | full` resolve to lane combinations that reproduce today's behavior exactly at every gate — verified site-by-site.

## User Impact

- **`/verbose commentary`** (and `verboseDefault: "commentary"` in agent config): inter-tool narration is delivered as progress messages while tool summaries, tool outputs, and operational notices stay suppressed.
- Existing levels and aliases are unchanged. Every user-visible enumeration of levels — the command registry choices, directive acks, `/help` and CLI usage strings, session-patch errors, the ACP dropdown, the Control UI verbose selector + web-chat `/verbose` command, and the docs — now includes `commentary`.
- Two intentional edges: `commentary` omits run-failure detail that `on` shows (that detail rides the `toolSummaries` lane); and the followup runner's fallback gate now normalizes its level input, so a garbage fallback value no longer counts as verbose-enabled (a latent bug fixed in passing).
- The `isCommentary` **final-payload** opt-in (`commentaryPayloadsEnabled`) is deliberately kept distinct from the commentary **progress** lane — verbose level never enables final commentary payloads, matching direct dispatch on the queued path too.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` both exit 0 (typecheck + oxlint + policy guards); `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched per CONTRIBUTING.
- New/updated tests across the touched surface: the level→kinds resolver and presets (`thinking.test.ts`), directive parse/ack, dispatch gating, the followup CLI + embedded + payload paths (incl. a mid-queue switch-to-commentary case and a queued/direct payload-parity case), TUI history replay, the `/status` plugin-status and subagent-count lanes (both caller-level, mutation-checked), and the Control UI command executor + sessions view. Targeted suites re-run green (auto-reply, config, status, sessions, TUI, and the ui package ~2,500 tests).
- Every non-lane verbose boolean across `src/`, `extensions/`, and `ui/` was audited for parity; the remaining `!== "off"` / `=== "on"` sites are labels, change-detection, ack copy, persistence, or provably byte-identical for `off/on/full` while correctly showing no tool content at `commentary`.

Verified on Node 24; re-validated on a second checkout at current `main`. **Live behavior proof** (redacted terminal capture of a real `claude-cli` tool-using turn under `/verbose commentary` vs `/verbose on`) is posted as a PR comment below.

Note: a couple of hunks in `thinking.test.ts` are `oxfmt`-driven (the file on `main` fails `oxfmt --check`); reverting them fails the formatter.

## Upgrade & Mixed-Version Compatibility

`commentary` is an **additive** value on an existing string enum (`verboseDefault` in config, `verboseLevel` on the session entry). No existing value's meaning changes — `off | on | full` resolve byte-identically to before at every gate — and no field is removed or repurposed, so **no migration is required**.

Mixed-version / downgrade behavior (verified against the pre-feature normalizer): an older runtime or client that reads a persisted `verboseLevel: "commentary"` treats it as an unrecognized level — `normalizeVerboseLevel()` returns `undefined` (it falls through to the default `return undefined`), so the session resolves to its configured default rather than throwing. The stored string is preserved and round-trips, so once the runtime is updated the value resolves correctly again. New code reading old persisted values behaves exactly as today.

Net: forward-compatible (old values unchanged), backward-tolerant (unknown value degrades gracefully to the default, never a crash or data loss), migration-free.

## AI-Assisted Disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude, via Claude Code) — reflected in the commit's `Co-Authored-By` trailer.

target.title: feat(google-meet): retain the full caption transcript per session (#103387)
target.body:
## Summary

Implements #103387.

The Chrome transport scrapes Meet captions into an in-page buffer capped at 50 lines, and `status` exposed only the last 5 as `recentTranscript` — so for any real meeting the transcript was mostly discarded, and observe-mode users had to build fragile external pollers that still lose lines during fast speech. This follows the accumulation design proposed in the issue.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/chrome.ts`: the status script now also ships its full in-page buffer as `transcriptWindow` (≤50 lines); `recentTranscript` stays at 5 lines for compatibility.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: the gateway merges `transcriptWindow` into a durable per-session transcript on every health refresh (join + status/health polls), deduped by the page-recorded `at`/`speaker`/`text` key, capped at the most recent **2000 lines** (fixed constant — no new config surface per the repo's config bar; `droppedLines` reports trimming). The window is merge input only and is stripped before health lands in status payloads, so `status` responses stay the same size. New `transcript(sessionId, { sinceIndex? })` refreshes browser health for active sessions and returns lines with absolute indices: `nextIndex` from one call is the `sinceIndex` for the next, which fixes the issue's "poll gap" problem exactly.
- `extensions/google-meet/index.ts`: new `googlemeet.transcript` gateway method and `transcript` tool action with optional `sinceIndex`.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts`: `openclaw googlemeet transcript <session-id> [--since <index>] [--json]`.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: observe-only section + tool action table updated.

Not included (flagged in the issue as optional): `chrome.transcriptFile` persistence — repo storage policy points that at SQLite rather than a JSONL sidecar, which is a separate product decision.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 207 tests passed. New regressions: overlapping page windows across polls accumulate without duplicates and the `sinceIndex` cursor returns exactly zero new lines at `nextIndex`; the cap test proves 2100 merged lines yield `droppedLines: 100`, retained lines 100..2099 in order (this test caught and fixed a dedupe-eviction bug during development); status payload health carries no `transcriptWindow`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt, oxlint — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: caption lines beyond a 5-line window over a 50-line page buffer were irrecoverable; no way to retrieve a meeting transcript after the fact.
Real environment tested: the plugin's real join/status/transcript gateway methods driven through the existing stubbed browser-proxy harness, with the page status script's real JSON contract (including the new `transcriptWindow`) exercised end to end.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet`
Evidence after fix: joining with page windows `[1..3]` then polling with `[2..5]` yields transcript lines 1..5 exactly once with `nextIndex: 5`; `sinceIndex: 5` returns no lines; a 2100-line window yields `droppedLines: 100` with lines 100..2099 retained in order.
Observed result after fix: 207/207 tests pass; the transcript survives beyond the page window and is retrievable incrementally via CLI, gateway method, and tool action.
What was not tested: a live Google Meet call with real captions; the merge consumes the same parsed status payload shape the live path produces, and the page-side change is a one-line widening of what the existing scraper already records.

target.title: fix(macos): reject revoked forwarded exec approvals
target.body:
Depends on #103950

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where delayed Gateway approval for a Mac App node could be rebound to freshly evaluated Mac policy. A rule revoked after upstream approval could therefore be restored by a later allow-always commit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node host now carries the canonical persisted-policy snapshot through both Mac execution routes: the authenticated exec socket and the native node session. The Mac requires the original snapshot for forwarded explicit and auto-review authority, revalidates it under the approval-store write lock, and rejects changed mutable script operands before execution.

Gateway no longer synthesizes delayed authority for nodes that omit `system.run.prepare`. It cannot prove remote executable or file identity from its own filesystem, so approval-requiring legacy native runs now fail closed before approval registration. Direct full/off execution remains unchanged.

Legacy boolean approvals normalize to one-shot socket decisions, and legacy allowlist source strings normalize to the portable `allow-always` contract before Swift decoding.

## User Impact

Mac App and CLI nodes now reject delayed approvals when policy is revoked while approval is in flight. Native nodes without prepare support receive a clear fail-closed error for approval-requiring runs instead of an unsafe Gateway-local plan. Local prompts, current-policy execution, ask-fallback ownership, and direct full/off execution are unchanged.

## Evidence

- clawmac native macOS run: 147 tests across five approval/runtime suites passed, including policy revocation, changed-script rejection, restored-byte execution, plan identity, and denial behavior.
- Follow-up native clawmac run: 115 tests across `ExecApprovalsStoreRefactorTests` and `MacNodeRuntimeTests` passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx79tebvg3g9rgnan3fwffcj`: 220 focused tests passed across agent node routing, node-host invocation, and approval-store suites.
- Same Testbox: `pnpm check:changed` passed in 8m08s, including typechecks, complete core lint shards, macOS packaging tests, import-cycle checks, and repository safety guards.
- Native i18n inventory check passed with 2,931 entries and no drift.
- SwiftFormat lint and targeted oxfmt checks passed.
- Exact-head CI repair at `99b2189300`: extracted the pure native plan/hash validator after SwiftLint caught `MacNodeRuntime.swift` over its 1,500-line limit; full Mac Swift lint, repository formatting, native i18n inventory, native package rebuild, and the 147-test clawmac suite passed.
- Fresh structured autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch judged correct (0.90).

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(cli): avoid zero usage cost during cache refresh
target.body:
Fixes #103882

AI-assisted: Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw gateway usage-cost --all-agents` could see `$0` during a cold aggregate-cache rebuild even though agent usage data existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway intentionally rebuilds aggregate cost caches in the background so large histories do not block a request for minutes. This keeps that behavior intact and makes the explicit CLI audit command poll with exponential backoff until the cache is settled, with a bounded five-minute timeout. Gateway protocol and Control UI behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

`gateway usage-cost` now prints settled totals once the cache rebuild completes, or exits with a clear timeout error instead of presenting a transient zero as the final result.

## Evidence

- Real CLI-to-Gateway before/after proof reproduced the transient zero on current `main` and returned settled nonzero totals on runtime commit `db846cf6d421`. Current head `594336c6ca1` changes only the regression test's callback typing; production content is identical.
- The regression test drives the real CLI command through the real `usage.cost` handler with two real agent transcripts. It observes `refreshing` first, `fresh` last, and verifies the final aggregate is `100` tokens / `$0.10`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts` — 2 files, 37 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -t 'rebuilds cold durable aggregate cache synchronously when requested'` — 1 passed, 68 skipped.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-103998-core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed after binding the regression callback to the real handler type.
- `oxfmt --check` and scoped `oxlint` passed for both changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- One pre-commit autoreview round completed with no actionable findings.
- Sanitized remote proof was unavailable because Crabbox has no configured coordinator, while credential-hydrated Testbox is intentionally disallowed for fork source. The documented narrow local fallback below used isolated, non-sensitive state.

### Real CLI ↔ Gateway proof

Setup: two fresh isolated state directories with no durable usage cache, two synthetic agents (`main` = 30 tokens / `$0.03`, `dev` = 70 tokens / `$0.07`), loopback-only `auth.mode=none`, and no provider credentials or calls. Each side ran a real foreground Gateway plus a separate real CLI process over WebSocket through the source-checkout entry (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`). Daily rows are omitted below; the shown totals and cache status are copied from the command output.

Current `main` at `f4b3a4841f2`, first cold request:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --all-agents --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 0, "totalCost": 0 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "refreshing",
    "cachedFiles": 0,
    "pendingFiles": 2,
    "staleFiles": 2
  }
}
```

PR runtime commit `db846cf6d421` (production-identical to current head `594336c6ca1`), first request against an equivalent cold state:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --all-agents --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 100, "totalCost": 0.1 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "fresh",
    "cachedFiles": 2,
    "pendingFiles": 0,
    "staleFiles": 0
  }
}
```

Representative explicit-agent request on the same PR Gateway:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --agent main --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 30, "totalCost": 0.03 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "fresh",
    "cachedFiles": 1,
    "pendingFiles": 0,
    "staleFiles": 0
  }
}
```

target.title: fix(google): Veo video generation fails with google-prefixed model ids
target.body:
Closes #103291

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where calling `video_generate` with a Google Veo model (e.g. `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`) fails with `API_KEY_INVALID` from the GenAI SDK, even though the same API key succeeds against the direct REST `predictLongRunning` endpoint with the `instances[].prompt` schema.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runtime already strips the `google/` provider prefix before forwarding the model id to the provider, so the provider receives the bare model name. The remaining failure is at the provider/SDK boundary: the GenAI SDK path for Veo models returns auth-style errors, while the existing REST fallback (which uses the correct `predictLongRunning` endpoint and schema) works.

This change:
1. Normalizes `google/`, `google/models/`, and `models/` prefixes to a bare Veo model id so both SDK and REST paths construct the correct `models/veo-...` URL.
2. Falls back to the REST `predictLongRunning` path for **any** SDK failure when the model is a Veo model and the request is text-only (the same condition that already allowed 404 fallback).

## User Impact

`video_generate` with `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, `google/models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, or `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` now routes through the working REST endpoint instead of failing on the broken SDK path.

## Evidence

### Shared-runtime regression

Added `src/video-generation/runtime.test.ts` regression verifying that the shared runtime strips the provider prefix from `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` and forwards the bare model id `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` to the provider.

Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/runtime.test.ts` — 29 tests passed.

### Provider behavior proof (SDK failure → REST success)

Added `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts` regression verifying that when the GenAI SDK rejects a Veo request with `API_KEY_INVALID` (status 400), the provider falls back to REST and hits `models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning` with the `instances[].prompt` schema, returning the generated video successfully.

Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts` — 19 tests passed.

### Direct-provider URL before/after

Intercepted the real provider code path with a stubbed API key and logged the outgoing URL:

**Before this change** (reverting to `HEAD~1`):
```text
[URL-PROOF] https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
```

**After this change** (current branch, `google/veo-...` normalized):
```text
[URL-PROOF] https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
```

The API key was redacted; no account, private endpoint, IP, or project id appears in the output.

### Note on live end-to-end proof

I do not have a live Google API key in this environment, so the before/after above exercises the real provider code path with intercepted HTTP. A maintainer with a Google key can verify by running `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test extensions/google/google.live.test.ts` or a live `video_generate` call.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:

```

```
Memory index updated (main).

```

```

Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
